Save traceable GBIF occurrences for local mapping

Source: R/spatial_gbif.R
gbif_save_occurrences.Rd

Resolves species as an exact, species-level GBIF name in the configured checklist (COL Extended Release by default) and retrieves georeferenced records using the resulting taxon key and the same checklist key. By default, up to 100,000 records are retrieved. Set limit = NULL to retrieve all available records. A finite limit is applied before any geographic crop. The function can optionally restrict records to a KML boundary, a named geographic area, or a WGS 84 bounding box. It saves the returned GBIF fields, machine-readable metadata including the exact name match and taxon key, and, for a crop, the corresponding WGS 84 boundary. Full-extent exports can be used offline with source = "local" in gbif_map() or gbif_map_crop(). A cropped export can be used with gbif_map_crop() by selecting source = "local", local_export = "crop", and the same crop arguments used when saving it. When both functions use the same taxon, occurrence set, and crop selectors, their saved occurrence records are interchangeable as local input. The default limit here is 100,000; use limit = NULL when the complete available occurrence set is required.

gbif_save_occurrences(
  species,
  kml = NULL,
  crop_area = NULL,
  crop_box = NULL,
  limit = 100000L,
  directory = getwd(),
  overwrite = TRUE
)

gbif_save_ocurrences(
  species,
  kml = NULL,
  crop_area = NULL,
  crop_box = NULL,
  limit = 100000L,
  directory = getwd(),
  overwrite = TRUE
)

Arguments

species

A binomial scientific name, for example "Bidens andicola". GBIF must resolve it as an exact species-level name; approximate or higher-rank matches are not used.

kml

Optional path to a .kml file used to restrict occurrences to a geographic area. It cannot be combined with crop_area.

crop_area, crop_box

Geographic crop selectors shared with gbif_map_crop(). They use the same area resolution, WGS 84 coordinate order, label, and overlap rules. Here they filter the records being saved and determine the Place subdirectory. crop_area cannot be combined with kml; crop_box can be used alone or with either boundary input.

limit

Maximum number of georeferenced records requested from GBIF before spatial filtering, as a positive integer from 1 to 100000. Defaults to 100000, as in gbif_map_crop(). Set to NULL to retrieve all available records. A saved crop may contain fewer records than a finite limit because the limit is applied before spatial filtering.

directory

Base output directory. As in gbif_map_crop(), the function creates sacha_exports/Family_Genus_species; cropped exports are placed in its Place subdirectory. Defaults to getwd().

overwrite

Logical. If TRUE (default), existing occurrence, metadata, and boundary files for this export may be replaced; FALSE prevents replacement.

Value

A named character vector with paths to the saved occurrence, metadata, and, for cropped exports, boundary files.

Details

Full-extent records are saved to sacha_exports/Family_Genus_species; cropped records are saved to sacha_exports/Family_Genus_species/Place, where Place is derived from the KML file name, the resolved geographic area, or the crop-box label (or its coordinates when no label is supplied).

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
gbif_save_occurrences("Bidens andicola")
gbif_save_occurrences("Bidens andicola", kml = "Cotopaxi.kml")
gbif_save_occurrences(
  "Bidens andicola",
  crop_box = c(-75, -10, -70, -5, "study area"),
  limit = 5000
)
gbif_map("Bidens andicola", source = "local")
} # }
